title: How the staffs are fired
summary: The three staffs in R.E.P.O. are built the same way: each one charges up with its own particles and sounds, reads as loaded, spawns a projectile from a point of its own, and carries a crystal, a screen arrow and a state to hold it all together.
body: The staffs differ in what they do, but they are fired the same way. Each one carries the same set of parts: particles for being loaded, for being refused and for charging up, and a state of its own to sit in.
A refusal is both seen and heard. Charging a staff that will not fire brings up refusal particles and a pair of sounds, one for the world and one for the interface, so the refusal is not silent.
Charging up is loud in its own right. There is a sound for the charge and a second one that loops while it is going on, which is why you can hear a staff being wound up before anything happens.
Firing has its own noise. A cast sound and a lightning sound belong to the moment of release, and two choir sounds belong to the effect alongside them.
A loaded staff keeps telling you so. There is a quiet loop for a low charge and a different loop for a high one, which is why the sound changes as the charge builds rather than staying level.
What leaves the staff is a projectile. There is a prefab for it and a point on the staff to spawn it from, so the shot comes from the object rather than from the middle of the screen.

Each staff is built around a crystal. The antigravity and torque staffs name a crystal material and renderers for it, while the void staff names mesh renderers, an emission gradient and a sphere collider of its own.
There are differences in the parts that move. The antigravity staff has a left and a right wing with a curve that drives them, and it also keeps a list of colliders to ignore while it works.
The void staff does something extra on impact. It names a second prefab to create when its shot lands, which is a part the other two do not carry.
Aiming is shown on screen. Every staff carries a screen arrow, so where the effect will go is drawn in the interface rather than left to guesswork.
The images beside this entry are the game's own: the colour artwork for the void staff and for the torque staff.
What this entry does not tell you: what a staff costs, how long a charge takes, or how strong any of the effects is. We have not verified those numbers, so we do not print them.

facts.claim: All three staffs carry particles for being loaded, refused and charged up, and a state of their own.
facts.evidence: identifiers: ItemStaffZeroGravity, ItemStaffVoid, ItemStaffTorque, loadedParticles, denyParticles, chargeUpParticles, currentState

facts.claim: A refused staff shows particles and plays a sound for the world and a separate sound for the interface.
Charging up has its own sound and a loop that runs while it does.
Firing plays a cast sound and a lightning sound, with two choir sounds belonging to the effect.
A loaded staff has a quiet loop for a low charge and a different loop for a high one.
The void staff has a set of loaded particles that stay active.
Each staff fires a projectile from a prefab and a spawn point of its own.
The void staff names a prefab to create when its shot lands.
The antigravity staff has a left and a right wing driven by a curve, and a list of colliders to ignore.
facts.evidence: identifiers: ItemStaffZeroGravity, wingTransformL, wingTransformR, wingAnimationCurve, ignoreColliders

facts.claim: Each staff has crystal artwork: a material and renderers, or mesh renderers with an emission gradient and a sphere collider.
facts.evidence: identifiers: crystalMaterial, crystalRenderers, crystalMeshRenderers, emissionGradient, sphereCollider, crystalRenderer

facts.claim: Every staff carries a screen arrow for aiming.
